To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) NLOS imaging is a challenging inverse problem with multiple solutions; (2) the global illumination component of time-resolved measurements contains sufficient information for shape reconstruction, even for objects that are partially occluded; (3) we introduce a novel formulation for the NLOS light transport, which models partial occlusion of hidden objects by visibility terms and (4) we demonstrate higher-fidelty reconstructions of partially-occluded objects using our formulation than previous methods.

(i) we introduce a new mathematical formulation for NLOS imaging that includes partial occluders, (ii) we demonstrate how to solve the inverse problem for this model and (iii) we demonstrate the performance gains of the new approach over previous methods.

(1) NLOS imaging can be achieved with visible objects, (2) the shape of hidden surfaces can be recovered with single-photon detectors and (3) the shape of objects hidden by partial occluders can be recovered using a new formulation of light transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new imaging methods for non-line-of-sight imaging.
the development of novel computational imaging methods that can be used to recover the shape and appearance of objects that are hidden from view.
the development and analysis of new imaging techniques for non-invasive imaging of objects hidden behind occluders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work provides a novel framework for NLOS imaging that enables the reconstruction of hidden scenes from a single view, even if the hidden objects are partially occluded by other visible objects.
our method is the best one in the field of NLOS imaging.
we have developed a novel formulation for non-line-of-sight imaging that models the light transport in a scene with partially occluded objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the global illumination components in the time-resolved measurements of a scene can be used for NLOS imaging.

we have developed an approach to NLOS light transport modeling, which is more accurate and more general than previous approaches, and which enables us to reconstruct the geometry of hidden objects with high fidelity.
the light transport from hidden objects to a camera can be modeled as a combination of the direct illumination and global illumination components of visible objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light transport in NLOS scenes is more complex than previously thought, but that it can be captured with the right model.
NLOS imaging can be used to reconstruct the shape and albedos of hidden objects even when the occluders are partially opaque.
NLOS imaging can be used for shape estimation of partially-occluded objects.
